15	#     rendered result with a different arrangement of ranges would not reproduce, so they are

18	#     rendered character through the public rendering API, so any implementation that paints the
19	#     same picture passes, whatever ranges it builds internally.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Behavioural verifier for textualize__textual-5826-mm.
#
# Restores the whole test tree from the immutable harbor_base tag, applies the discriminating
# tests from test.patch, runs them, and computes a BINARY reward (1.0 only when every f2p and
# every p2p passes).
#
# NEVER greps candidate source for the fix -- it runs the tests.
#
# Two test files carry the scored tests:
#   tests/test_markup.py          -- the repository's own markup suite, extended by the upstream
#     fix with new parameter sets. Only its two implementation-neutral cases are scored as p2p
#     (an unrelated markup case, and the unbalanced-markup error path). Its remaining cases
#     compare the exact list of styled ranges, which a correct fix that describes the same
#     rendered result with a different arrangement of ranges would not reproduce, so they are
#     deliberately left unscored: they run, but they cannot cause an invalid failure.
#   tests/test_markup_nesting.py  -- the scored tests. They assert the effective style of every
#     rendered character through the public rendering API, so any implementation that paints the
#     same picture passes, whatever ranges it builds internally.
set -uo pipefail

mkdir -p /logs/verifier
STDOUT_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stdout.txt
STDERR_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stderr.txt
REPORT=/logs/verifier/report.xml
: > "$STDOUT_LOG"; : > "$STDERR_LOG"; rm -f "$REPORT"

# Anti-cheat: the agent runs before the verifier and shares /logs. A reward file planted there
# would survive the ensure_reward trap below (which only writes when the file is ABSENT) if the
# verifier died early, and a verdict.json planted in the judge dir wins outright over the API
# backend (judge.py resolves an existing verdict first, which is what makes a rescore
# idempotent), handing out a rubric pass with nothing graded. Clear all of it before scoring.
rm -f /logs/verifier/reward.txt /logs/verifier/reward.json
rm -rf /logs/verifier/judge

ensure_reward() { [ -f /logs/verifier/reward.txt ] || echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt; }
trap ensure_reward EXIT

cd /app || { echo "no /app" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# ── Restore the ENTIRE test tree from harbor_base ────────────────────────────────────────────
# Everything under tests/ is writable by the agent, so resetting only the two files test.patch
# touches would still leave a planted tests/conftest.py able to stub out to_content or the
# rendering API for the whole run. Resetting the tree, then cleaning untracked leftovers, closes
# that at once; --noconftest below closes the same hole for a conftest planted outside tests/.
echo "== restoring tests/ from harbor_base ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
git -C /app checkout harbor_base -- tests/ 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || {
    echo "ERROR: could not restore tests/ from harbor_base" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }
git -C /app clean -fdq -- tests/ 2>/dev/null || true

# Robustness + idempotency for anything test.patch touches outside tests/ (nothing today).
# Read paths from `diff --git a/... b/...` headers, which are present for text, BINARY, renamed
# and deleted entries -- NOT from `+++ b/`, which is ABSENT for binary and renamed entries.
_patch_paths=$(
  { sed -n 's#^diff --git a/\(.*\) b/.*#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
    sed -n 's#^diff --git a/.* b/\(.*\)#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
  } | sort -u )
for _p in $_patch_paths; do
  git -C /app checkout harbor_base -- "$_p" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "/app/$_p" 2>/dev/null || true
done

echo "== applying test.patch ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
git apply /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || patch -p1 -i /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || { echo "ERROR: could not apply test.patch" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# ── Install the test runner, at verify time and offline ──────────────────────────────────────
# The image ships no test tooling, so the agent's environment carries nothing it would not need
# to write the fix. The wheels were resolved and frozen into the image at build time, so this
# install is pinned, offline and identical on every run: no registry is contacted here, and a
# registry outage cannot turn a correct fix into a reward of 0.0.
echo "== installing pinned test runner from the offline wheel cache ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
python -m pip install --no-index --find-links=/opt/test-wheels --quiet pytest==8.3.4 \
  >>"$STDOUT_LOG" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || { echo "ERROR: could not install pytest from /opt/test-wheels" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# ── Run the suite ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# --noconftest      : neither test file needs a conftest, so none is loaded -- a planted one
#                     (at the repository root, where the base tree has none) cannot run.
# -o addopts=       : neutralises any addopts injected into the project's pytest configuration.
# -p no:cacheprovider : no .pytest_cache is written into the checkout between runs.
echo "== running markup tests ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
python -m pytest tests/test_markup.py tests/test_markup_nesting.py \
  --noconftest -o addopts= -p no:cacheprovider \
  --junitxml="$REPORT" --tb=short -q --no-header \
  >>"$STDOUT_LOG" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || echo "(tests exited non-zero; parsing report)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

echo "== rubric judge (graded in band when the API backend is reachable; never fatal) ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
RUBRIC=""
if [ -f /tests/rubrics.json ]; then
  RUBRIC=$(python3 /tests/judge.py --rubrics /tests/rubrics.json --repo /app 2>/logs/verifier/judge.log || echo "")
  echo "Rubric verdict: ${RUBRIC:-pending (judge request written; rescore after grading)}" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
fi

echo "== computing reward ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
python3 /tests/verifier.py --rubric "${RUBRIC:-}" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
echo "reward=$(cat /logs/verifier/reward.txt 2>/dev/null)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

+"""Rendered-appearance tests for overlapping and nested markup tags.
+
+These tests deliberately assert what the terminal ends up painting -- the effective style
+of every single character, after all the styled ranges have been layered on top of each
+other -- instead of asserting the exact list of ranges a particular implementation happens
+to build. Two implementations may describe the same picture with different ranges (one wide
+range with narrower ones layered over it, or a run of adjacent non-overlapping ranges), and
+both are correct as long as each character is painted the same. Only `to_content` and the
+public rendering API are used, so nothing here depends on how the spans are assembled.
+
+Expected colours are resolved through `Style.parse` rather than written as literal hex, so
+the assertions stay valid regardless of the palette behind a colour name.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import pytest
+
+from textual.markup import to_content
+from textual.style import Style
+
+
+def paint(markup: str) -> list[tuple[str, str | None]]:
+    """Render `markup` and return (character, effective foreground colour) for each character."""
+    painted: list[tuple[str, str | None]] = []
+    for text, style in to_content(markup).render(end=""):
+        for character in text:
+            foreground = style.foreground
+            painted.append((character, None if foreground is None else foreground.hex))
+    return painted
+
+
+def colour(style: str) -> str | None:
+    """The foreground colour a style string resolves to, as rendered."""
+    foreground = Style.parse(style).foreground
+    return None if foreground is None else foreground.hex
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Nesting: the tag closest to a character is the one that shows.
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def test_nested_colors_paint_each_character() -> None:
+    """Three colours opened one inside the other paint three different characters."""
+    assert paint("[blue][green][red]R[/red]G[/green]B[/blue]") == [
+        ("R", colour("red")),
+        ("G", colour("green")),
+        ("B", colour("blue")),
+    ]
+
+
+def test_nested_hex_colors_paint_each_character() -> None:
+    """The same nesting written with hex colours instead of names paints the same way."""
+    assert paint("[#ff0000][#00ff00][#0000ff]A[/#0000ff]B[/#00ff00]C[/#ff0000]") == [
+        ("A", colour("#0000ff")),
+        ("B", colour("#00ff00")),
+        ("C", colour("#ff0000")),
+    ]
+
+
+def test_sibling_tag_inside_nesting_paints_each_character() -> None:
+    """A second tag opened after an inner tag closed keeps the enclosing colours intact.
+
+    Also mixes the two ways of closing a tag: by name, and with the bare closing tag.
+    """
+    assert paint("[blue][green][red]R[/red][yellow]Y[/]G[/green]B[/blue]") == [
+        ("R", colour("red")),
+        ("Y", colour("yellow")),
+        ("G", colour("green")),
+        ("B", colour("blue")),
+    ]
+
+
+def test_innermost_tag_wins_for_properly_nested_pair() -> None:
+    """When two tags wrap the same character and nest cleanly, the inner one shows."""
+    assert paint("[red][blue]X[/blue][/red]") == [("X", colour("blue"))]
+
+
+def test_first_closed_tag_wins_for_crossed_pair() -> None:
+    """When two tags wrap the same character and are closed out of order, the tag closed
+    first is the one that shows -- whether the second tag is closed afterwards or left open.
+    """
+    assert paint("[red][blue]X[/red][/blue]") == [("X", colour("red"))]
+    assert paint("[red][blue]X[/red]") == [("X", colour("red"))]
+
+
+def test_tags_that_wrap_nothing_produce_no_spans() -> None:
+    """Markup whose tags end up wrapping no text at all yields empty content with no
+    styled range covering an empty stretch of text.
+
+    Every form is checked together because they are one property: a tag that never gets any
+    text under it, whether it is closed by name, closed with the bare closing tag, or left
+    open to the end of the markup.
+    """
+    for markup in [
+        "",
+        "[bold]",
+        "[bold][/]",
+        "[bold][/bold]",
+        "[red][green][/red]",
+        "[red][green][/]",
+    ]:
+        content = to_content(markup)
+        assert content.plain == "", markup
+        empty_spans = [span for span in content.spans if span.start == span.end]
+        assert empty_spans == [], f"{markup!r} produced {empty_spans!r}"
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Regression guards: behaviour that already worked and must keep working.
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def test_unclosed_tags_stack_innermost_on_top() -> None:
+    """Two tags opened over the same character and never closed: the inner one shows."""
+    assert paint("[red][blue]X") == [("X", colour("blue"))]
+
+
+def test_cascading_unclosed_tags_paint_each_character() -> None:
+    """Tags opened one after another and never closed each take over from where they start."""
+    assert paint("[blue]A[green]B[red]C") == [
+        ("A", colour("blue")),
+        ("B", colour("green")),
+        ("C", colour("red")),
+    ]
+
+
+def test_closing_a_tag_restores_the_enclosing_one() -> None:
+    """Text after an inner tag closes goes back to the colour that is still open around it."""
+    assert paint("[blue]start[red]mid[/red]end[/blue]") == [
+        *[(character, colour("blue")) for character in "start"],
+        *[(character, colour("red")) for character in "mid"],
+        *[(character, colour("blue")) for character in "end"],
+    ]
+
+
+def test_auto_closed_tag_leaves_following_text_unstyled() -> None:
+    """Text after a tag is closed with nothing else open around it carries no style at all."""
+    painted = paint("[bold red]Hello[/] World")
+    assert painted[:5] == [(character, colour("bold red")) for character in "Hello"]
+    assert painted[5:] == [(character, None) for character in " World"]
+    trailing = [style for text, style in to_content("[bold red]Hello[/] World").render(end="")
+                if text.endswith("World")]
+    assert trailing and all(style.bold is None for style in trailing)
+
+
+def test_adjacent_tag_pairs_paint_their_own_range() -> None:
+    """Two tag pairs written back to back colour their own character and nothing else."""
+    assert paint("[red]A[/red][green]B[/green]") == [
+        ("A", colour("red")),
+        ("B", colour("green")),
+    ]
+
+
+def test_non_conflicting_attributes_combine() -> None:
+    """A colour and an attribute wrapping the same character both survive."""
+    (text, style), *rest = to_content("[blue][bold]N[/bold][/blue]").render(end="")
+    assert text == "N"
+    assert rest == []
+    assert style.foreground is not None
+    assert style.foreground.hex == colour("blue")
+    assert style.bold is True
+
+
+def test_unbalanced_markup_is_still_rejected() -> None:
+    """Closing tags with nothing to close, or closing a tag that was never opened, still fail."""
+    from textual.markup import MarkupError
+
+    with pytest.raises(MarkupError):
+        to_content("foo[/]")
+    with pytest.raises(MarkupError):
+        to_content("[foo]foo[/bar]")

132	    so a permissive substring match could silently score the wrong test. A non-unique hit is
133	    reported as 'ambiguous' and never counts as a pass, making the misconfiguration loud.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Report -> reward for textualize__textual-5826-mm.

Parses the JUnit XML report produced by test.sh (pytest --junitxml) and computes the reward
from config.json's f2p/p2p identifiers. It NEVER inspects candidate source for the behavioural
half of the score: it only reads the test report.

Reward policy (tests, BINARY, no partial credit):
  1.0 -- every f2p test passes AND every p2p test passes
  0.0 -- anything else (a strict subset of f2p, a p2p regression, a suite that failed to run,
         a skipped test, or an identifier that matched no test)

Rubric gate: test.sh forwards the judge verdict via `--rubric pass|fail`. A "fail" verdict forces
the reward to 0.0 even when every test passes. A "pass" or unavailable verdict (judge not graded
yet, or an empty value) never lowers the score, so oracle and nop runs are unaffected by a judge
that did not run.

Identifier matching: pytest appends a "-content<N>" counter to the ids of the parametrized
`test_to_content` cases, because several parameter sets stringify to the same id fragment. The
counter is an artefact of the parameter list's ORDER, so it is stripped before matching -- a
candidate that leaves the test file alone (the only supported case; test.sh restores it anyway)
still matches, and the configured identifiers stay readable.

IMPORTANT: this script WRITES /logs/verifier/reward.txt (bare float) and /logs/verifier/reward.json.
reward.json MUST stay a FLAT map of numbers: harbor validates it as dict[str, float | int] and
prefers it over reward.txt; a nested dict/list/string/None raises a validation error that aborts
the trial before any reward is recorded.
"""
import argparse
import atexit
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

CONF = json.load(open('/tests/config.json'))
F2P, P2P = CONF['f2p'], CONF['p2p']

REPORT = '/logs/verifier/report.xml'
_CANON_TXT = '/logs/verifier/reward.txt'
_CANON_JSON = '/logs/verifier/reward.json'
RUBRIC_SUMMARY = '/logs/verifier/judge/summary.json'

# "test_to_content[[bold red]Hello[/] World-content6]" -> "test_to_content[[bold red]Hello[/] World]"
PARAM_COUNTER_RE = re.compile(r'-content\d+\]$')

# Worst outcome wins when one identifier resolves to several reported results.
_RANK = {'pass': 0, 'skip': 1, 'fail': 2}

# --- canonical reward writer -------------------------------------------------
# The seven mandatory keys, plus one flat scalar per test (f2p::<name> / p2p::<name>).
# The per-test keys surface in harbor's result.json metrics, which is what lets the gate audit
# confirm that every f2p individually fails on the untouched base.
_canon = {}


def canon_reward(f2p_statuses, p2p_statuses, rubric):
    f = sum(1 for v in f2p_statuses.values() if v == 'pass')
    p = sum(1 for v in p2p_statuses.values() if v == 'pass')
    t, q = len(f2p_statuses), len(p2p_statuses)
    solved = bool(t) and f == t and p == q
    tests_passed = 1.0 if solved else 0.0
    _canon.clear()
    _canon.update({
        'reward': 0.0 if rubric == 'fail' else tests_passed,
        'tests_passed': tests_passed,
        'f2p_passed': f, 'f2p_total': t,
        'p2p_passed': p, 'p2p_total': q,
        'rubric_passed': {'pass': 1, 'fail': 0}.get(rubric, -1),
    })
    for name, status in f2p_statuses.items():
        _canon['f2p::%s' % name] = 1.0 if status == 'pass' else 0.0
    for name, status in p2p_statuses.items():
        _canon['p2p::%s' % name] = 1.0 if status == 'pass' else 0.0
    return _canon['reward']


@atexit.register
def _canon_flush():
    if not _canon:
        return
    try:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(_CANON_JSON), exist_ok=True)
        with open(_CANON_JSON, 'w') as fh:
            json.dump(_canon, fh, indent=2)
        with open(_CANON_TXT, 'w') as fh:
            fh.write(str(_canon['reward']))
    except Exception as exc:
        print('WARNING: could not write %s: %s' % (_CANON_JSON, exc), file=sys.stderr)


def load_results():
    """Return {test_name: 'pass'|'fail'|'skip'} parsed from the JUnit XML report.

    Both the raw pytest id and the id with the parametrize counter stripped are recorded, so a
    configured identifier matches either form. A name reported more than once keeps its worst
    outcome, so neither a duplicate nor a collision after stripping can mask a failure.
    """
    results = {}
    if not os.path.exists(REPORT):
        return results
    try:
        tree = ET.parse(REPORT)
    except ET.ParseError as exc:
        print('WARNING: could not parse %s: %s' % (REPORT, exc), file=sys.stderr)
        return results

    def record(name, status):
        previous = results.get(name)
        if previous is None or _RANK[status] > _RANK[previous]:
            results[name] = status

    for testcase in tree.iter('testcase'):
        name = testcase.get('name', '')
        if not name:
            continue
        failed = any(child.tag in ('failure', 'error') for child in testcase)
        skipped = any(child.tag == 'skipped' for child in testcase)
        status = 'skip' if skipped else ('fail' if failed else 'pass')
        record(name, status)
        record(PARAM_COUNTER_RE.sub(']', name), status)
    return results


def match_ident(ident, results):
    """Resolve one configured identifier to 'pass' | 'fail' | 'skip' | 'missing' | 'ambiguous'.

    Exact name first. Only if there is no exact name does this fall back to substring matching,
    and that fallback demands a UNIQUE hit: the suite contains test names that are strict
    prefixes of other test names (`test_to_content` is a prefix of `test_to_content_variables`),
    so a permissive substring match could silently score the wrong test. A non-unique hit is
    reported as 'ambiguous' and never counts as a pass, making the misconfiguration loud.
    """
    if ident in results:
        return results[ident]
    hits = {name: status for name, status in results.items() if ident in name}
    if len(hits) == 1:
        return next(iter(hits.values()))
    if len(hits) > 1:
        return 'ambiguous'
    return 'missing'


def rubric_failed_ids():
    """Failed criterion ids from the judge summary, when one exists."""
    if os.path.isfile(RUBRIC_SUMMARY):
        try:
            return json.load(open(RUBRIC_SUMMARY)).get('failed', [])
        except Exception:
            return []
    return []


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument('--rubric', default='', help='"pass" | "fail" | "" (no verdict yet)')
    args = ap.parse_args()
    rubric = (args.rubric or '').strip().lower()
    rubric = rubric if rubric in ('pass', 'fail') else None

    results = load_results()
    f2p_statuses = {ident: match_ident(ident, results) for ident in F2P}
    p2p_statuses = {ident: match_ident(ident, results) for ident in P2P}

    reward = canon_reward(f2p_statuses, p2p_statuses, rubric)

    print(json.dumps({
        'reward': reward,
        'tests_passed': _canon['tests_passed'],
        'rubric': rubric,
        'rubric_failed': rubric_failed_ids(),
        'f2p': f2p_statuses,
        'p2p': p2p_statuses,
        'f2p_passed': _canon['f2p_passed'], 'f2p_total': _canon['f2p_total'],
        'p2p_passed': _canon['p2p_passed'], 'p2p_total': _canon['p2p_total'],
        'parsed_tests': len(results),
    }, indent=2))
    print('\nREWARD: %s' % reward)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Rubric judge: API backend, with the sub-agent request as fallback.

Binary and unweighted: every criterion is PASS/FAIL and every one is mandatory, so the
rubric passes only if all pass.

Grading, in order:

  1. API backend (during the verifier run)
      If EVAL_API_KEY/EVAL_BASE_URL/EVAL_MODEL are all set (via [verifier.env] in task.toml,
      which also needs [verifier] network_mode = "public"), the diff is graded in-band against
      the proxy and verdict.json is written immediately, so the run's own reward.json carries
      rubric_passed without any manual follow-up.

  2. Sub-agent fallback (during the verifier run, when the API is unavailable)
      Writes a self-contained judge request into the judge dir -- criteria_payload.json,
      source.txt (the candidate diff), changed_files.txt (the FULL text of every file the diff
      touched), and PROMPT.md -- prints nothing, and exits 0. The verifier then scores on tests
      alone until a human grades PROMPT.md and reruns rescore.

  3. Phase 2 rescore (after the run, orchestrated outside the container)
      Only reached if both of the above left no verdict. A judge sub-agent reads PROMPT.md and
      writes verdict.json next to it. Re-running this script (or `mm_run.sh <task> rescore`)
      reads that verdict and prints "pass" or "fail".

Both backends are handed exactly the same inputs, so they cannot disagree on the evidence.
What is deliberately withheld from both: the golden solution/fix.patch (seeing it turns the
judge into a similarity checker, reintroducing the very overfitting the rubric exists to
catch), tests/test.patch (same failure mode, and the tests already score that), and the
screenshots (UI-evaluation criteria are out of scope by definition).

No credential is ever written into this file or the bundle -- EVAL_API_KEY etc. are ${VAR}
references in task.toml, expanded by harbor from its own environment at run time.

Contract (test.sh depends on all three):
  * prints "pass" or "fail" on stdout, or NOTHING when no verdict is available yet
  * writes the per-criterion detail to <judge dir>/summary.json
  * ALWAYS exits 0, so the judge can never fail the run

Env:
  PB_JUDGE_DIR      where the request/verdict live (default /logs/verifier/judge)
  PB_JUDGE_VERDICT  explicit path to verdict.json (overrides the default location)

IMPORTANT: never name a file in tests/ after a stdlib module (select.py, json.py, types.py,
io.py, queue.py). It shadows the real module and the failure surfaces somewhere unrelated.
The sys.path strip below defends against it.
"""
import os
import sys

_self_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path[:] = [p for p in sys.path if os.path.abspath(p or os.getcwd()) != _self_dir]

import argparse
import json
import re
import subprocess
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

DEFAULT_JUDGE_DIR = "/logs/verifier/judge"
# Hunks for these paths never reach the judge: it must grade the fix, not the harness the
# submission may have edited.
EXCLUDE_RE = re.compile(
    r"(\.test\.[jt]sx?$|\.spec\.[jt]sx?$|(^|/)tests?/|(^|/)__tests__/|"
    r"(^|/)__snapshots__/|(^|/)node_modules/|(^|/)\.git/)"
)
BASE_REFS = ("harbor_base", "HEAD")

JUDGE_SYSTEM = (
    "You are a strict senior engineer grading the APPROACH of a code change -- not whether "
    "its tests pass. Score each rubric criterion STRICTLY BINARY: 1 = fully satisfied, "
    "0 = not satisfied. There is NO partial credit: if a criterion is only partially met, "
    "ambiguous, or has no clear evidence, score 0. Be strict; when unsure, score 0."
)

# Bounded well inside the 2400s verifier timeout even in the worst case
# (API_ATTEMPTS * API_TIMEOUT_SEC + backoff).
API_TIMEOUT_SEC = 300
API_ATTEMPTS = 3


def build_user_prompt(criteria, diff: str, changed: str) -> str:
    """The API-backend counterpart of PROMPT.md, with the same inputs and exclusions.

    Deliberately withheld, exactly as in the sub-agent request: the task instruction, the
    golden fix.patch, tests/test.patch, and the screenshots.
    """
    payload = json.dumps(
        [{"id": c["id"], "criterion": c["criterion"]} for c in criteria], indent=2
    )
    ids = ", ".join(c["id"] for c in criteria)
    parts = [
        "Grade the APPROACH of the code change below against each rubric criterion.",
        "",
        "## Criteria",
        payload,
        "",
        "## Candidate diff (test/spec/snapshot files already stripped)",
        "```diff",
        diff,
        "```",
    ]
    if changed.strip():
        parts += [
            "",
            "## Full current text of every file the diff touched",
            "Use this when a hunk alone is too little context to decide a criterion.",
            changed,
        ]
    parts += [
        "",
        "## Output",
        'Reply with JSON only, no prose and no code fences: {"scores": {"<id>": 0 or 1}}.',
        f"All {len(criteria)} ids must be present: {ids}.",
        "Score 1 only when the criterion is fully satisfied with clear evidence in the "
        "change; otherwise score 0. There is no partial credit.",
    ]
    return "\n".join(parts)


def extract_scores_object(text: str):
    """Parse the model reply into a dict, tolerating fences and surrounding prose."""
    candidate = text.strip()
    if candidate.startswith("```"):
        candidate = re.sub(r"^```[a-zA-Z]*\n?", "", candidate)
        candidate = re.sub(r"\n?```$", "", candidate.strip())
    try:
        return json.loads(candidate)
    except Exception:
        pass
    start, depth = None, 0
    for i, ch in enumerate(candidate):
        if ch == "{":
            if start is None:
                start = i
            depth += 1
        elif ch == "}" and start is not None:
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                try:
                    return json.loads(candidate[start : i + 1])
                except Exception:
                    start, depth = None, 0
    return None


def call_eval_api(criteria, diff: str, changed: str):
    """Grade via the proxy. Returns a scores-shaped dict, or None to fall back.

    Never raises: every failure path returns None so the caller can fall through to the
    sub-agent request and the run is never failed by the judge.
    """
    api_key = (os.environ.get("EVAL_API_KEY") or "").strip()
    base_url = (os.environ.get("EVAL_BASE_URL") or "").strip().rstrip("/")
    model = (os.environ.get("EVAL_MODEL") or "").strip()
    if not api_key or not base_url or not model:
        sys.stderr.write(
            "[judge] API backend unavailable (EVAL_API_KEY/EVAL_BASE_URL/EVAL_MODEL "
            "incomplete); falling back to the sub-agent request\n"
        )
        return None

    body = {
        "model": model,
        "temperature": 0,
        "messages": [
            {"role": "system", "content": JUDGE_SYSTEM},
            {"role": "user", "content": build_user_prompt(criteria, diff, changed)},
        ],
    }
    # The proxy attributes spend per `user`; without it this call is unattributable.
    if os.environ.get("EVAL_USER"):
        body["user"] = os.environ["EVAL_USER"]

    url = base_url + "/chat/completions"
    data = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8")
    for attempt in range(1, API_ATTEMPTS + 1):
        try:
            req = urllib.request.Request(
                url,
                data=data,
                method="POST",
                headers={
                    "Authorization": "Bearer %s" % api_key,
                    "Content-Type": "application/json",
                },
            )
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=API_TIMEOUT_SEC) as resp:
                raw = resp.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            content = json.loads(raw)["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
            obj = extract_scores_object(content)
            if not isinstance(obj, dict):
                sys.stderr.write(
                    "[judge] attempt %d: reply was not JSON: %r\n" % (attempt, content[:400])
                )
            else:
                sys.stderr.write("[judge] graded via API model=%s\n" % model)
                return obj
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            detail = ""
            try:
                detail = exc.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")[:400]
            except Exception:
                pass
            sys.stderr.write(
                "[judge] attempt %d: HTTP %s %s\n" % (attempt, exc.code, detail)
            )
            # 4xx other than 429 will not fix themselves; stop retrying.
            if 400 <= exc.code < 500 and exc.code != 429:
                break
        except Exception as exc:
            sys.stderr.write(
                "[judge] attempt %d: %s: %s\n" % (attempt, exc.__class__.__name__, exc)
            )
        if attempt < API_ATTEMPTS:
            time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
    sys.stderr.write("[judge] API backend gave up; falling back to the sub-agent request\n")
    return None


def judge_dir() -> Path:
    return Path(os.environ.get("PB_JUDGE_DIR") or DEFAULT_JUDGE_DIR)


def candidate_diff(repo: str, budget: int = 120_000) -> str:
    for ref in BASE_REFS:
        try:
            out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "diff", ref],
                                 capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
        except Exception as exc:
            sys.stderr.write("[judge] git diff failed: %s\n" % exc)
            return ""
        if out.returncode == 0 and out.stdout.strip():
            sys.stderr.write("[judge] diffing against %s\n" % ref)
            return filter_diff(out.stdout, budget)
    sys.stderr.write("[judge] no non-empty diff found\n")
    return ""


def filter_diff(diff: str, budget: int) -> str:
    kept, cur, keep = [], [], True
    for line in diff.splitlines(keepends=True):
        if line.startswith("diff --git "):
            if keep and cur:
                kept.extend(cur)
            parts = line.split()
            path = parts[-1][2:] if len(parts) >= 4 else ""
            keep = not EXCLUDE_RE.search(path)
            cur = [line]
        else:
            cur.append(line)
    if keep and cur:
        kept.extend(cur)
    blob = "".join(kept)
    return blob[:budget] + "\n[... truncated ...]\n" if len(blob) > budget else blob


def changed_paths(diff: str) -> list:
    """Paths touched by the (already harness-filtered) diff, in order."""
    out = []
    for line in diff.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("diff --git "):
            parts = line.split()
            if len(parts) >= 4:
                p = parts[-1][2:]                  # strip the b/ prefix
                if p and p not in out:
                    out.append(p)
    return out


def collect_changed_files(repo: str, diff: str, budget: int = 200_000) -> str:
    """Full current text of every file the diff touched.

    A hunk shows three lines of context, which is often too little to decide a criterion that is
    genuinely true of the change. This task is a live example: the one-line fix reads a value
    whose definition sits several lines ABOVE the hunk, so a judge given only the hunk cannot see
    where that value comes from and, told to score 0 when unsure, would fail a correct change.
    Whole files remove that class of false 0 while staying bounded by the size of the change.
    """
    blob, used = [], 0
    for rel in changed_paths(diff):
        fp = Path(repo) / rel
        if not fp.is_file():                       # deleted or renamed away
            continue
        try:
            text = fp.read_text(errors="replace")
        except Exception:
            continue
        chunk = "\n===== %s =====\n%s" % (rel, text)
        if used + len(chunk) > budget:
            blob.append("\n[... remaining changed files omitted for length ...]\n")
            break
        blob.append(chunk); used += len(chunk)
    return "".join(blob)


def write_request(criteria, diff, jdir: Path, changed: str = "") -> None:
    """Lay down everything a judge sub-agent needs, with no further context.

    Same inputs as the API backend (see build_user_prompt), so the two cannot disagree.
    """
    jdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # Explicit utf-8 on every write: the container's locale decides Path.write_text's default
    # codec, and this template is not pure ASCII. A UnicodeEncodeError here would take the whole
    # judge down, which is exactly what the "never fatal" contract forbids.
    payload = [{"id": c["id"], "criterion": c["criterion"]} for c in criteria]
    (jdir / "criteria_payload.json").write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    (jdir / "source.txt").write_text(diff, encoding="utf-8")
    extra = ""
    if changed.strip():
        (jdir / "changed_files.txt").write_text(changed, encoding="utf-8")
        extra = ("\n- `changed_files.txt`: the FULL current text of every file the diff touched. "
                 "Use it when a hunk alone is too little context to decide a criterion.")
    verdict = jdir / "verdict.json"
    ids = ", ".join(c["id"] for c in criteria)
    (jdir / "PROMPT.md").write_text(f"""# Rubric judge (sub-agent)

You are the rubric judge. Grade the APPROACH of a code change, not whether its tests pass.

System contract:
{JUDGE_SYSTEM}

Inputs in this directory ({jdir}):
- `criteria_payload.json` — {len(criteria)} criteria, each {{id, criterion}}.
- `source.txt` — the candidate diff. Test, spec and snapshot files are already stripped out,
  so everything you see is product code the submission changed.{extra}

You are NOT given the reference/golden fix, the tests, or the screenshots. Judge only what is
here. If a criterion cannot be decided from these inputs, score it 0, but note that a criterion
which is undecidable here is a defect in the rubric, not in the submission.

Score each criterion **1 or 0 — never 0.5 or any fraction**. 1 = fully satisfied,
0 = not satisfied, ambiguous, or no clear evidence. Be strict; when unsure, score 0.

The rubric is unweighted and every criterion is mandatory: a single 0 fails the whole rubric,
so do not withhold a 1 over style preferences the criterion does not actually state.

Write ONLY this JSON to `{verdict}`:

    {{"scores": {{"<criterion id>": {{"score": 0|1}}, ...}}}}

All {len(criteria)} ids must appear: {ids}. Verify the file parses before you finish.
""", encoding="utf-8")


def read_verdict(criteria, jdir: Path):
    """Return ("pass"|"fail", failed_ids) or None when no usable verdict exists."""
    vp = Path(os.environ.get("PB_JUDGE_VERDICT") or (jdir / "verdict.json"))
    if not vp.is_file():
        return None
    try:
        obj = json.loads(vp.read_text())
    except Exception as exc:
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict unreadable (%s)\n" % exc)
        return None
    scores = obj.get("scores", obj)
    if not isinstance(scores, dict):
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict has no scores map\n")
        return None
    failed, graded = [], 0
    for c in criteria:
        raw = scores.get(c["id"])
        if raw is None:
            failed.append(c["id"])            # not graded == not demonstrated == fail
            continue

            v = float(raw.get("score") if isinstance(raw, dict) else raw)
        except (TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError):
            failed.append(c["id"])
            continue

        if v < 1.0:                            # strictly binary: only a full 1 passes
            failed.append(c["id"])
    if graded == 0:
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict contained no usable scores\n")
        return None
    return ("fail" if failed else "pass"), failed

    """One scoring path for both backends: write summary.json, print, exit 0."""

        jdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        json.dump({"rubric": verdict, "failed": failed,
                   "criteria_total": len(criteria)},
                  open(jdir / "summary.json", "w"), indent=2)
    except Exception:
        pass
    sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict=%s%s\n"
                     % (verdict, (" failed=%s" % ", ".join(failed)) if failed else ""))
    print(verdict)
    return 0


def main() -> int:

    ap.add_argument("--rubrics", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--repo", default="/app")
